It Takes a Village: Understanding Cost Share on Sponsored Projects

Hello MSU Faculty & Staff! In this module we will review key pre and post-award processes related to Cost Share, a.k.a. matching, at Morgan State University. Topics include proper cost share documentation practices, identifying sources of cost share, distinguishing between various types of cost share, and more. Please note that processes detailed in this module are specific to grant-funded activities. Some of the information may also be relevant to non-sponsored activity actions; however, policy and procedural differences may apply. We strive to continuously review these lessons to provide up-to-date guidance on Morgan's sponsored project processes. For questions related to the activities covered in this module that are not addressed in the module content, please contact the ORA Training and Communications Coordinator: Mr. Ryan Mobley, CRA, CFRA, CPRA Email: ryan.mobley@morgan.edu Phone: 443-885-4771 Thank you, ORA Training Team

Self-paced ORA eTraining module. Source: https://share.articulate.com/jQ-qp8p2axC-3ba_0hXae

Before diving into the specifics of cost sharing at Morgan State University, it’s essential to address a fundamental question: What exactly is cost share?

Cost share, also known as matching, refers to the portion of a project’s costs that are not covered by the sponsor of the award and are instead borne by MSU or a third party. For example, a private company may offer a piece of equipment to a MSU faculty member for work on a project. Or MSU may partially cover salary costs for project personnel. Assets offered for cost sharing must be allowable and directly allocable to the project (ie. utilized directly to further the goals of the project). Additionally, these resources cannot be derived from previous or active federal funding for cost sharing on federal grants.

Forms of Cost Share

Cost sharing can be structured in various forms, each tailored to meet specific project or grant requirements, including direct financial contributions, in-kind support like equipment or services, dedicated personnel time, or waived indirect costs. To qualify as cost share, these contributions must be allowable under the funding opportunity announcement (FOA) and directly allocable to the project.

Non-cash contributions such as facilities, equipment, or supplies.
In-Kind Contributions
Actual dollars allocated to the total project budget.
Cash Contributions
Salary and fringe costs for the effort of faculty & technical staff not charged to the sponsor, but contributes directly to the success of the project.
Effort
When such costs are used for advancing the goals of the project but are not reimbursed by the sponsor.
Graduate Student Salaries or Tuition Remission
A reduction of MSU’s negotiated F&A cost recovery. However, only some federal agencies allow for this form of cost sharing.
Unrecovered F&A

Cost sharing cannot be allocated to more than one project in full. For example, if Morgan State University supports 25% of a faculty member's time as cost share, it is permissible to allocate this time across multiple projects, such as 15% toward one project and 10% toward another. However, applying the full 25% to multiple projects is not allowed. Similarly, for equipment used in cost sharing, usage hours should be tracked and reported separately for each project to ensure accurate allocation.

Let's explore the different ways institutions can contribute to sponsored projects: mandatory, voluntary committed, and voluntary uncommitted cost share. Understanding these distinctions is essential for effective project planning and compliance with funding requirements.
text aside
LIGHT
DEFAULT
interactive
https://cdn.articulate.com/assets/rise/assets/block-defaults/paraglide_thumb.jpg
Mandatory Cost Share
Mandatory cost share is the portion of project or program costs that a grant recipient, such as a university or research institution, is required to contribute as a condition of receiving certain federal or other types of funding. This contribution is stipulated by the funding agency and is usually specified in the funding opportunity announcement or award terms. Mandatory cost share must be honored and properly documented .
Voluntary Committed Cost Share
Voluntary committed cost share is when MSU, in the project proposal and associated budget and budget justification, voluntarily offers to contribute to the project when not required by the sponsor. Once the proposal is approved by the sponsor it becomes a binding obligation. Voluntary committed cost share must be honored and properly documented . Please Note : As a rule, MSU forbids voluntary committed cost share. Voluntary committed cost share generally does not increase a project’s chance of being funded. This type of cost share may also be explicitly prohibited by the FOA. PIs seeking to provide voluntary committed cost share must receive approval from their Chair, Dean, and the Office of Research Administration prior to proposal submission.
Voluntary Uncommitted Cost Share
If cost sharing occurs during the execution of the award, but is not mandated by the FOA or promised in the proposal, it is considered voluntary uncommitted cost share . For instance, if a Principal Investigator (PI) dedicates 35% of their time to a project instead of the 25% originally committed, with the additional 10% covered by the university, this would constitute voluntary uncommitted cost sharing. Since this additional effort is neither required nor formally pledged, it does not represent a binding obligation. There is no mandate for documentation or reporting to the sponsor.

Pre Award Planning
heading
WHITE
ACCENT
image
Cost sharing at Morgan State University is a significant, long-term commitment that spans the entire lifecycle of a project, from inception through closeout. Meeting these obligations is essential to maintain federal compliance and uphold our institutional commitment to supporting research. Carefully review the following steps to ensure that all necessary actions are taken prior to submitting any proposal with cost-sharing requirements.
impact
LIGHT
Cost Share: Pre-Award Phase
All proposals for sponsored projects must be routed through ORA prior to submission. The Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR) is the only individual authorized to submit applications and accept awards on behalf of MSU.
note
interactive
Step #1: Submit an Internal Routing Form (IRF)
For any proposal submission, a prospective PI must complete an Internal Routing Form (IRF) to provide necessary preliminary information to ORA & the Office of Restricted Funds Accounting (RFA). When a project has mandatory or voluntary committed cost share the PI must check the corresponding box on the IRF.
Step #2: Review Budget with ORA Budget Specialist
During the proposal preparation phase, the ORA Budget Specialist will review the FOA and IRF. If cost share commitments are present, they will ask the PI for elements of cost share and will work with the PI to prepare a budget and budget justification. These documents will be included in the proposal submission.
Step #3: Chair & Dean Approval
If an award has mandatory or voluntary committed cost share, the budget and budget justification must be approved by the PI’s Chair and Dean and provided to the ORA no later than one week prior to the project’s submission deadline.
Step #4: 3rd Party Cost Share
For third party cost share, the PI will be required to provide ORA & RFA with documentation detailing the commitment from the external entity. The PI should provide this documentation no later than one week prior to the proposal submission deadline. Valuation of 3rd party cost share should be in line with market value for similar goods & services.

Post Award: Documentation and Monitoring
heading
WHITE
ACCENT
image
Congratulations on receiving your award! With the Notice of Award (NOA) now in hand, it's essential to establish cost share commitments from day one. To facilitate this, please review the following steps carefully to ensure cost share is accurately recorded in Banner. Proper tracking is critical for accurate sponsor invoicing and maintaining federal fiscal compliance.
impact
LIGHT
Cost Share: Post-Award Phase
interactive
Step #1: Initial Award Setup
When the Office of Research Administration receives an NOA with committed cost share the following will happen: A post award briefing will be scheduled with DRED staff, the PI, and their support staff. The briefing will provide resources, allow for questions, and detail the requirements and responsibilities of cost share under the award. ORA Staff will coordinate with Restricted Funds Accounting (RFA) staff to create a Cost Share Activity Code. Use of the activity code is covered later in this lesson.
Step #2: Cost Share Specifics Sent to RFA
The ORA Budget Specialist will send the cost share budget and budget justification to the RFA team.
Step #3: Host a Post Award Briefing
A post award briefing is required for all projects with documented cost share. We will outline the requirements and responsibilities of cost share and determine cost share sources. The project's cost share activity code will be shared with the PI via the RFA team.
Step #4: Complete Cost Share DocuSign Forms
For personnel cost share, a Payroll Cost Share Memo (attached below) must be completed and sent to Crystal Nichols (crystal.nichols@morgan.edu). This form should be completed for any personnel (PI, Co-PI, Program Manager, etc) whose salary will require cost share under the award. It is crucial to verify an employee does not over commit cost share between all projects at MSU. Please review your payroll cost share memo with your RFA account prior to submitting the completed form to Ms. Nichols. For non-personnel cost share, the appropriate Non-Payroll Cost Share Form (below) must be completed on a schedule outlined by the PI's RFA Grant Accountant. This schedule will be based on the invoicing/reporting deadlines of the award. There are two Non-Payroll Cost Share Forms: Non-Payroll Cost Share Memo - Participant Support Costs Non-Payroll Cost Share - Travel, Services, & Commodities

Step #5: Cost Share Activity Code
As a part of the award setup process the MSU RFA team will create a cost share activity code specific to each award. The code typically will reflect the project's fund code with a 'C' at the end. For example, a project with fund code 12345 would have a cost share activity code of 12345C. The code can be used on a variety of expensing instruments to include travel forms, stipend requests, requisitions, and p-card reconciliations. Below are examples of where the activity code would be used for p-card reconciliations and requisitions.
